scope: Huddle chat contracts moved from the removed POST /api/calls/:id/chat/messages to the gateway socket send on orgiq:huddle:<callId> (join, send with clientDeliveryId, persisted 'sent'); native contracts re-run; burst x1 + soak x1 unchanged; count/timing-only per-stage send profile; one reversible change (DM conversation index written once) A/B measured
driverFinding: scripts/loadtest/realtime-calls.mjs never called the removed REST route: its chat leg is the gateway socket send on social:dm:<a>:<b> (join/send/message frames). The burst/soak chat p95 numbers measure real socket DM sends, not the dead route, so the driver was left unchanged (changing it to huddle chat would change the workload the plugin-scope table compares against).

contractChanges.meaning: Each former POST now joins the seat's socket to orgiq:huddle:<callId> and sends the portal's frame; success = the echoed message carrying the delivery id plus the library 'sent' for that id; any error frame on the channel fails the step. Peer delivery, durable history (GET /:callId/chat), retired-epoch non-delivery, crash/rejoin, Redis owner replacement and Dynamo outage assertions are unchanged. Added: a same-user unseated socket on the peer BFF is refused join/send, receives no huddle frames and stores nothing; replacement connections rejoin like the portal does.

contracts.redisFaults: 2/3 in two runs (redis-failures-1.log, redis-failures-2.log). Both huddle-chat cases pass. The failing case sends no chat: after the paused-Redis fence, realtime:orgiq-bff-cluster-acceptance:node:bff-b keeps being renewed by a live client (EVAL PEXPIRE every ~8 s, redis-stall-lease-renewal-monitor.txt) while both health endpoints stay 503, so 'old stable owner leases expire naturally' times out. Reproduced 2/2; passed in plugin-scope. Not diagnosed here.
contracts.dynamoFault: 1/1 (dynamo-failures.log). A first attempt failed at connect because the Redis stall failure leaves both native BFFs fenced (no restart in its failure path); it passed after the guarded helper restart.
contracts.nativeBffs: restarted only through test-support/bff-cluster-processes.py (processes.log); final owned PIDs in /tmp/orgiq-bff-cluster-{a,b}.pid

stageProfile.method: test-support/native-rds-preload.mjs (bind-mounted, metrics file only): AsyncLocalStorage stage labels around ChatService.handleSendMessage/_checkMembership/_persistMessage/broadcastMessage, channelAccess.routerPermits, LocalRealtimeRouter.allows/fanOut/sendFiltered, RedisRealtimeRouter.checkChannel/publish/receive and each router plugin; Dynamo calls attributed to the innermost stage; http.request socket-assignment splits pool wait from DynamoDB Local service time. Counts/timings only. The instrumentation itself slows the run (instrumented burst chat p95 5,822.8 vs 3,272.1 plain), so stage numbers rank causes; they are not the plain-run latency.
ranked: 1. DynamoDB SDK socket-pool wait. 50 sockets per node, activePeak 50, queuedPeak 1,463/1,323. Per Dynamo call on the send path the wait is 168-595 ms against 36-52 ms DynamoDB Local service time (~90% of each call is queueing). Event loop p99 stays 45-51 ms, so the loop is not the bottleneck.

2. Pool demand per send: ~17 pool requests per stored message. Largest single category: chat-conversations UpdateItem 4.0 per DM send (2,696/675 node a), avg 718 ms, written twice for the same two rows (library store.chatOptions onChannelMessage AND the host's social:dm index).

3. Recipient authorization on fan-out: router.authorize.subscribe 5,502 checks (1,845 chat-members queries, avg 215 ms) and redisRouter.peerReceive 5,713 (954 queries, avg 260 ms) - the peer side of every delivery waits in the same pool.
4. Publish authorization repeated per send: routerPermits.publish ~4.6 per send (avg 181 ms) + checkChannel.publish; membership reads share via the scope but each check still awaits.
5. Persist PutItem avg 233 ms (wait 171 + service 47); broadcast avg 544 ms (local fan-out + peer publish 60 ms).

Unattributed: driver delivery p50 (3.8 s instrumented) exceeds send.total (1.46 s) + peerReceive (0.26 s); the remainder is before handleSendMessage starts (frame dispatch/queueing) and was not instrumented.

change.what: middleware/src/lib/realtime-gateway.ts createSocialChatBackend.chatOptions: for tenant DM channels (social:dm:) the host's name-derived conversation index replaces the library's channel-hook index instead of running beside it; every other channel still uses the library hook. Regression assertion in src/lib/__tests__/realtime-gateway-social-dynamo.test.ts (exactly one UpdateItem per member; fails 2 extra without the change). Gateway/call-chat/social-embedded suites: 160 passed, 6 skipped.

measured.verdict: Removes redundant writes and halves the pool queue, but end-to-end burst chat p95 does not improve beyond run-to-run noise (~±600 ms). Not a capacity fix; kept because it is correct and tested. Revert with the diff if unwanted.
